description: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking perturbations across different linguistic tags for various multilingual BERT models. The horizontal axis represents the categories, labeled "tag," and includes four discrete groups ordered from left to right: "case," "gender," "number," and "tense." The vertical axis, labeled "effect," measures the numerical value on a linear scale with tick marks and corresponding horizontal gridlines at intervals of 5, spanning a labeled range from 0 to 20, though error bars extend below 0 and above 20. Within each of the four tag categories, there is a grouped set of six adjacent vertical bars representing different models, as specified by a legend in the top right corner. From left to right within each group, the bars are identified as "mBERT-L₂" in light blue, "XLM-L₂" in dark blue, "mBERT-R₂" in light green, "XLM-R₂" in dark green, "mBERT-B₂" in light red, and "XLM-B₂" in dark red. Each bar is visually outlined in black and features a vertical black error bar with horizontal caps, indicating standard deviation. The bars are not sorted by height but maintain the consistent six-model sequence within each grouping. The largest effects are found in the "case" category, which contains the tallest bar, "mBERT-B₂," reaching an approximate value of 12.2 with a substantial error bar extending up to roughly 21. In contrast, the shortest bars are located in the "tense" category, where values are nearly zero; the "XLM-L₂" and "XLM-R₂" bars sit flat at approximately 0, and the "mBERT-R₂" bar dips slightly below the baseline to approximately -0.1.
